transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-12 14:30 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Alex, Rina, Sara, Ben, Evan

Summary section (auto-gen, may be rough): quick sync on onboarding, infra, security docs, and bench anomalies.

00:00 Alex: okay thanks everyone for joining, um we'll try to keep to 45 but there's a couple of blockers so we might run a bit over. intro, alex chen from Redwood, rina is our solutions eng.
00:14 Sara: hi all, sara here, running point for seed model tests, quick note we had one failed job overnight that I want to flag.
00:22 Rina: yep saw that in the logs, looks like the runner timed out when KV cache attempted recovery, possibly due to connection churn over the peered link.
00:35 Ben: yeah we haven't completed the vpc peering, sorry that was supposed to be done last night, ran into a firewall policy from our side.
00:46 Alex: okay that makes sense. so action item — Ben to finish peering and open the gateway port, without that the ded-icated gateway (redwood dedicate, sometimes shows as redwood ded-site in logs) will fail auth handshakes.
00:58 Evan: quick security interjection — we need to confirm KMS usage and whether tokenized logs still contain SSNs in plaintext. can you share the audit log format?
01:10 Alex: yes, we'll send the SOC2 excerpt and the audit-log schema. quick heads up the log names in our console are sometimes abbreviated e.g., rwinf-audit which is the redwood inferencing console name in older exports.
01:26 Sara: about the failed job, latency spiked to 2.8s per token on a 1k prompt set which is higher than expected; baseline was 1.2-1.4s in the initial run.
01:38 Rina: that spike could be a cold cache effect plus batching change — we changed batch size to 8 overnight to reduce cost but that can increase p99 latency. did you run with prefix cache warm?
01:50 Sara: no we didn't set cache warm flag, we were using the default.
01:55 Rina: ok we'll re-run with cache warm and continuous batching disabled for the p99 sweep. also will check kv cache timeouts, sometimes the ttr value is set low.
02:08 Ben: question — what's the recommended egress path? do we push through your managed gateway or direct peering? we want minimal hops for latency but also must satisfy our compliance routing.
02:20 Alex: recommend peering for production tests — lowest latency. managed gateway is quicker to start but may add a hop and some egress NAT. for the pilot, peering for the benchmark runs then switch to dedicated gateway for controlled testing is a good pattern.
02:36 Evan: regarding keys, our KMS is AWS-managed, we need to ensure Redwood can reference the key via role assumption, not key export. is that supported?
02:49 Rina: yes we support role-based access and we integrate with KMS via encrypt-at-rest only, no key export. RFC in our docs shows sample roles, but we'll send a concrete example.
03:02 Sara: any blockers on certs? we tried to upload the client cert but the dashboard threw a 400 and the cert name might've had a space.
03:12 Alex: oh yeah the cert name parser is, um, picky — avoid spaces and unusual chars. we can accept pem, p12 formats. we'll add a note in the runbook.
03:24 Ben: I'll re-run the peering config tonight and post the ticket. also need to know if we should open port 9443 or 443 for the peered path.
03:36 Rina: for peering open 9443 to the Redwood gateway ip ranges we provided; 443 is used for managed gateway. we'll attach the ip list in the runbook.
03:48 Sara: about SLOs — our product team expects <200ms median and <800ms p95 for user flows. is that realistic?
04:00 Alex: for hosted small models yes, but for the large sequence lengths you're running, 200ms median is unlikely without heavy quantization or pinned dedicated GPUs. we discussed quant profiles earlier, we can recommend q4nh or q5 on nodes and run a cost/latency tradeoff.
04:19 Sara: okay we're primarily concerned with cost vs latency; product can accept higher p95 if median is good. we'll document tradeoffs.
04:29 Evan: any compliance docs we should expect? we need SOC2, ISO27001, and an audit log extract.
04:36 Alex: we'll share SOC2 excerpt and audit-log schema today; ISO and full attestation are available via our sales portal for enterprise customers — will flag that in the shared folder.
04:48 Ben: question on creds: service account vs token rotation, what's the best practice?
04:54 Rina: use service account with short-lived tokens, rotate via Vault or AWS STS. we support both patterns; we'll include sample policies.
05:05 Sara: timeline check — we're aiming to complete infra and run the 1k prompt sweep by Monday. can Redwood re-run with cache warm and send results mid next week?
05:15 Alex: yep Rina will handle the re-run and we'll schedule a short result review on Tuesday.
05:23 Evan: last note, we may bring in our compliance lead next week for a deeper security walk-through.
05:30 Alex: great — recap: Redwood sends security pack + runbook, SE redoes bench with cache warm, FinNova finishes peering and provides KMS ARNs, and we meet next Tuesday for results. thanks all.

End of transcript. Some portions of transcript may contain mis-transcribed product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated") and truncated log labels.
questions: Can Redwood support role-based KMS access without key export?
Is peering required for initial benchmark runs or can we use managed gateway?
What's the recommended quantization profile for 2x latency improvement?
